editorial.headline: Other Annual Crops, With Bali Depending on the Exact Scope
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to foreign ownership, but Bali registration turns on the risk profile declared in OSS for the precise activity.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01199 is a residual but important agricultural activity: it covers annual crop farming that is not otherwise classified, including planting activities aimed at producing seed in the form of grain. In operational terms, the scope is not limited to the crop standing in the field. It reaches the full basic cycle described in the record: preparing and processing land, sowing, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and post-harvest processing. It also includes seed activities for other annual crops that fall within this same residual category.

That breadth matters because this is the kind of code a founder may look at when the real activity is agricultural but does not sit neatly under a narrower label. The registrant could be small or large: the record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%, under the stated source Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no foreign-stake cap in the slim record below full ownership, so the national reading is straightforward: a foreign-owned company can in principle use this activity at the permitted scale.

Bali is the part that requires more careful handling. The record does not mark this activity as absolutely blocked for Bali; `l4_bali_blocked` is false. But the Bali status is not a clean open signal either: it is BLOCCATO_DIPENDE_SCOPE. The reason given is precise and should shape the founder's expectations. OSS risk at scale Besar is low on some scopes, but higher on others, and registration as a PMA in Bali is available only by declaring the higher-risk scope. That means the practical question is not merely whether the national investment list is open. It is whether the exact activity entered in OSS lands on a risk profile that Bali will accept for PMA registration.

The background rule is strict: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanently, with the source recorded as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. For this code, that does not produce a blanket no, but it does make the declared scope decisive. The honest reading is therefore conditional: nationally open, potentially registrable in Bali, but only if the live OSS declaration for the exact activity carries the higher-risk scope described in the record. A founder should treat the crop activity, the seed activity, the scale, and the OSS risk outcome as one joined question, not as separate boxes to tick.
